newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG says Schimmelbusch deal not on agenda.
newsitem.headline: MG says Schimmelbusch deal not on agenda.

text.p: Plans for an out-of-court settlement between Metallgesellschaft AG and its disgraced former chairman Heinz Schimmelbusch are not on the agenda for its supervisory board meeting, an MG spokesman said.

The spokesman declined to comment further on press reports claiming that an out-of court settlement had been agreed with Schimmelbusch, who has been blamed for leading MG to the brink of bankruptcy in late 1993.
"We do not have an agenda point called 'Settlement with Schimmelbusch' on the agenda for Friday," an MG spokesman said in answer to enquiries.

A report in the weekly Welt am Sonntag Sunday newspaper and other press reports said that the MG supervisory board is to meet on January 31 to discuss a settlement for Schimmelbusch and MG's former finance director Meinhard Forster.

Both officials left the company after billions of marks of losses on risky oil deals in the United States were uncovered, forcing banks to step in an bail out the company with a 3.4 billion rescue deal.
Schimmelbusch in particular has hotly contested accusations that his hedging strategy -- which secured long-term deliveries with short-term futures -- was a recipe for disaster.

The Welt am Sonntag report said MG was now prepared to accept an out-of-court settlement with Schimmelbusch that would guarantee his pension of 340,000 marks ($207,000) from the age of 65 and assume all of his legal fees resulting from the company's suit for damages against the former chief executive.

MG looked close to a court fight with the former chief last July when it responded to a long document from Schimelbusch spelling out why he believed accusations against him were misplaced by saying the issue now belonged in court.

At that stage, its supervisors rejected an initial out-of-court settlement worked out between the lawyers working for the two sides. Formal charges against Schimmelbusch have not been filed. ($ = 1.636 German Marks)
